description: Uniform flow past a smooth sphere, Re = U*D/nu = 100, D3Q19 + MRT + Bouzidi interpolated (sub-cell smooth) bounce-back wall + far-field BC. Cd taken from the BFL per-link momentum ledger (laboratory frame) summed over the wall-adjacent boundary links -- a surface-restricted caliber on a SMOOTH interpolated wall. Two grids (D=40/D=60) within 3% of Schiller-Naumann and monotonically convergent (span 0.231%).
geometry: parametric sphere, radius 0.5, mask on the analytic sphere; wall = Bouzidi-Firdaouss-Lallemand interpolated bounce-back (compute_q_sphere gives the sub-cell wall distance q per boundary link)
force_method: BFL per-link momentum ledger (laboratory frame), bfl_force_ledger_sparse, summed over wall-adjacent boundary links only. This is the pre-registered judgment observable (NOTES.md sec 7). The wall is a sub-cell SMOOTH interpolated boundary (not a staircase), which removes the doubly-curved staircase geometry bias that makes the alternative staircase Ladd-MEM caliber fail (+9%).

domain_convergence_signature.note: BFL route error is dominated by the upstream inlet distance (far_field_bc_3d Dirichlet clamping). err vs up/D at lat 2.0: err ~ E0 + C*(a/x)^3 (R^2=0.9998). Enlarging the domain (lat 2->3, up 1.25->3, down 2.25->4) moves the error inside the 3% gate.

alternative_caliber_staircase_ladd_mem.summary: Staircase sphere + half-way bounce-back + surface-only Ladd MEM (cylinder_3d caliber) converges to +9% -- a mesh-converged geometry bias, NOT a caliber bug.
alternative_caliber_staircase_ladd_mem.domain_lever_dead: lateral 16 vs 32 at D=10: step-1000 cd_mem_surface = 1.3177 vs 1.3178 (bit-identical 4dp)
alternative_caliber_staircase_ladd_mem.cv_cross_check: control-volume momentum balance agrees: D=16 1.1985 (+9.8%), D=20 1.2130 (+11.1%)
alternative_caliber_staircase_ladd_mem.cylinder_3d_contrast: cylinder is singly curved (invariant in z), surface-only caliber brings it into the reference cluster (+1.62%/-0.99%); the sphere is DOUBLY curved with interior/total = 0.62 (D12) / 0.71 (D18), so the same caliber only trims +12.7% to +9.15%. Only a smooth/interpolated boundary representation (the BFL route used here) removes the bias.

acceptance: every checkpoint within 3% AND mesh-converged (two grids, span <=3%); sphere_re100 satisfies both (2.771%/2.540%, span 0.231%) AND |err| monotone decreasing
reproduction: cd benchmarks/verified/sphere_re100 && CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<id> PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True python run.py --D 40 --steps 12000 --lat 3.0 --up 3.0 --down 4.0 --tau 0.56 --sample 50 --cv_tail 2500   # then --D 60 --tau 0.59 --steps 24000; python verify.py
